{
  "//": "THE TEST DIRECTORIES `pnpm typecheck` NEVER REACHES - THE SHARED HALF. Every `<pkg>/tsconfig.test-dirs.json` - beside the package's own program, NEVER inside the test directory it reads - extends this file; `scripts/typecheck-test-dirs.mjs` compiles each of them on its own and holds the result against `test/typecheck-test-dirs.baseline.json`. None of it is in any package program: `tsc -b` follows references and every referenced project includes `src` only. The files are named `tsconfig.test-dirs.json` rather than `tsconfig.json` DELIBERATELY - vite/esbuild take their per-file transpile settings from the nearest `tsconfig.json` and search for that name alone, so a config named this way cannot change how the suite runs the very files it reads. They sit beside the package rather than inside `test/` because `apps/desktop/test` is a PUBLISHED payload root with an extension filter, and the mirror runs its own CI over what lands there: a `.json` inside it is either a file the mirror omits (an incomplete published tree) or one it ships dangling on a private base config. `apps/sidecar/tsconfig.tests.json` has always sat there for the same reason.",
  "//paths": "THE ROOT VITEST ALIAS TABLE, MIRRORED, AND IT IS NOT DECORATION - the same reasoning `apps/sidecar/tsconfig.tests.json` spells out. Without it `@trafficflow/core` in a test resolves through node_modules to `packages/core/dist/*.d.ts`, the BUILT declarations, so these programs would check the tests against whatever was last compiled instead of against the source vitest runs: a stale dist hides the errors this exists to find, and a fresh one reports errors against a different program than the suite executes. `scripts/typecheck-test-dirs.mjs` imports `vitest.config.ts` and refuses to run when one `find` in that table has no key here or points at a different file. The paths are relative to THIS file (`test/`), because TypeScript resolves a relative path against the config it is written in, not against the one that extends it.",
  "//composite": "`false`, overriding the base. A composite project may not disable emit (TS6304), and these programs emit nothing.",
  "//noEmit": "Nothing is written. These are readers.",
  "extends": "../tsconfig.base.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "noEmit": true,
    "composite": false,
    "declaration": false,
    "paths": {
      "@trafficflow/core/adapters/http-host": ["../packages/core/src/adapters/http-host.ts"],

{
  "//": "THE TEST DIRECTORIES `pnpm typecheck` NEVER REACHES - THE SHARED HALF. Every `<pkg>/tsconfig.test-dirs.json` - beside the package's own program, NEVER inside the test directory it reads - extends this file; `scripts/typecheck-test-dirs.mjs` compiles each of them on its own and holds the result against `test/typecheck-test-dirs.baseline.json`. None of it is in any package program: `tsc -b` follows references and every referenced project includes `src` only. The files are named `tsconfig.test-dirs.json` rather than `tsconfig.json` DELIBERATELY - vite/esbuild take their per-file transpile settings from the nearest `tsconfig.json` and search for that name alone, so a config named this way cannot change how the suite runs the very files it reads. They sit beside the package rather than inside `test/` because `apps/desktop/test` is a PUBLISHED payload root with an extension filter, and the mirror runs its own CI over what lands there: a `.json` inside it is either a file the mirror omits (an incomplete published tree) or one it ships dangling on a private base config. `apps/sidecar/tsconfig.tests.json` has always sat there for the same reason.",
  "//paths": "THE ROOT VITEST ALIAS TABLE, MIRRORED, AND IT IS NOT DECORATION - the same reasoning `apps/sidecar/tsconfig.tests.json` spells out. Without it `@trafficflow/core` in a test resolves through node_modules to `packages/core/dist/*.d.ts`, the BUILT declarations, so these programs would check the tests against whatever was last compiled instead of against the source vitest runs: a stale dist hides the errors this exists to find, and a fresh one reports errors against a different program than the suite executes. `scripts/typecheck-test-dirs.mjs` imports `vitest.config.ts` and refuses to run when one `find` in that table has no key here or points at a different file. The paths are relative to THIS file (`test/`), because TypeScript resolves a relative path against the config it is written in, not against the one that extends it.",
  "//composite": "`false`, overriding the base. A composite project may not disable emit (TS6304), and these programs emit nothing.",
  "//noEmit": "Nothing is written. These are readers.",
  "extends": "../tsconfig.base.json",
